The real unit's focus setting and its corner sharpness are unknown (unsourced); a slanted-edge measurement from the owner would settle them.
items.proposed_change: (1) Give the onboard PinholeCameraCfg f_stop = 2.8 and a focus_distance (default: the hyperfocal 0.83 m; make it a flag --focus_m) and enable rtx_look.OPTIONAL['dof'] for these cameras only if the key is registered (apply() already warns). Test only at ground, liftoff and final, where it matters. (2) Replace the constant blur with a field-dependent sigma in sensor_sim.optics: sigma(r) = sigma0 + (sigma_corner - sigma0) * r^2 with sigma_corner chosen from the owner's measurement (start 0.5 -> 1.0 px, an assumption, unsourced).
items.risk: The DoF setting has no visible effect at 40 m and may cost frame time; the key '/rtx/post/dof/enabled' is unverified for Kit 107. More blur lowers the sharpness metrics: coordinate with camera-aa-resample-sharpness and do not tune both blindly. No map rebuild.
sources: real lens focus and MTF: unsourced

items.title: The recording loop never waits for textures and models to stream in, so low-resolution textures or missing objects may appear as the drone moves 2 km
items.current: SimulationManager.assets_loading() is polled only before the first frame (30 renders, then up to 3000 renders, lines 733-740) and, in probe mode, after each jump to a moment (line 495, whose comment says 'textures and models streaming in near here'). The video loop (lines 742-790) renders every 8th physics step as fast as the GPU allows and never checks it again. The map is a single 'AddReference' of world.usdc (line 558) whose trees and grass reference NVIDIA https URLs. Whether textures, mip levels or instances arrive late along the route is unverified.
items.real_world: Not a real-world number: a real camera never shows a texture sharpening or an object popping in. Probe stills cannot reveal this because the probe code already waits at every moment.
items.proposed_change: Instrument first: in the record loop add the value of SimulationManager.assets_loading() and the wall time of each captured frame to the per-frame records written into camera_info.json (records[name] dict, line 704). Then record a 60 s cruise segment twice: as now, and with 'while assets_loading(): sim.render()' (cap 3000) before each captured frame. Compare the two with realism/metrics.py (spectral slope of consecutive frames, frame-to-frame SSIM drops) and by eye on the first frames of each new region. If pop-in is confirmed keep the per-frame wait; optionally pre-warm by flying the route once at 4x without capture.
items.risk: The per-frame wait slows rendering; if assets_loading() never becomes false (a missing asset) keep the 3000 cap. Needs a video segment, not stills. No map rebuild. If streaming is not an issue on the GPU PC the item can be closed after the instrumentation.

items.title: Ground and roof colour has no information below 10 m: lots, driveways, garden beds, bare patches, pools and individual roofs are invented, although NAIP aerial imagery is already fetched for comparison
items.current: Ground albedo = class texture x one Sentinel-2 median tint per class x a brightness factor per 25 m Voronoi patch (45 m for crops), clamped 0.75-1.3 and quantised into 6 variants (build.py:220-265). The finest colour source is Sentinel-2 at 10 m (data.sentinel(frame, far, 10.0, ...), build.py:551). Roof and wall style are a hash of the footprint centroid (buildings.py:61-95). realism/reference.py already reads NAIP from Microsoft Planetary Computer, but only to cut comparison squares.
items.real_world: The repo's own docstring (realism/reference.py:1-3) says NAIP is '0.6 m or finer; flown in summer, leaves on' (claimed by the repo, not verified in this session). That is about 17x finer per axis than the 10 m Sentinel-2 grid (computed: 10 / 0.6). A typical suburban lot being 20-30 m wide is unsourced. Everything on a lot (drive, shed, bed, pool, bare patch, a differently coloured roof) is below the current colour model's resolution.
items.proposed_change: In world/data.py add naip(frame, rect, res=0.6) reusing realism/reference.cut and signed(). Keep Sentinel-2 as the radiometric truth and use NAIP only for structure: ratio = NAIP_luma(0.6 m) / gaussian_blur_to_10_m(NAIP_luma), clamped to 0.5-1.8, multiplied into the face tint (the terrain cells are 1 m near the route, so a per-vertex colour primvar or a per-tile low-resolution multiply texture is enough; UsdPreviewSurface cannot multiply two textures, so bake the ratio into per-tile copies of the albedo or use displayColor). Mask NAIP's own baked shadows (pixels below about 0.5 x the local median) so the renderer's shadows are not applied twice. For roofs, replace the hash slot choice in buildings.style by the NAIP median colour inside each footprint (nearest of the existing slots, then calibrate_tints). Validate on the nadir stills with metrics.py --pairs against the NAIP squares.
items.risk: Needs BUILD_VERSION (build.py:48) and TEXTURE_VERSION bumps and a map rebuild. NAIP DNs are not calibrated reflectance and carry shadows from the acquisition sun, hence the ratio-only use. Acquisition year and Overture/Meta canopy dates differ. More download volume (not cached by reference.py). Supersedes the fix suggested for ground-patch-quilt if adopted.

items.title: Railways are discarded: a rail line crossing the area would be bare ground
items.current: data.roads() keeps only Overture segments with subtype 'road' ((sub[i] or 'road') != 'road' is skipped, data.py:110; the docstring says 'rail and water lines dropped'). A railway therefore shows up only if a 'railway' land-use polygon exists (landcover.py:35, mapped to SOIL); there is never ballast, track or sleepers. The 'rail_flags' column is requested in the reader but unused.
items.real_world: Whether a railway lies inside the 12 km map or crosses the 2 km route in west Ames is unverified (an offline check on the PC: intersect the cached Overture segment table with subtype 'rail'; drop this item if there is none within about 3 km of the route). Standard gauge 1.435 m and a ballast bed of about 3.5-4 m are from memory and unsourced.
items.proposed_change: In data.roads keep subtype 'rail' segments as a separate list; in roads.py add a rail builder: a ballast ribbon 3.5 m wide (desaturated crushed-stone material, e.g. NVIDIA Soil_Rocky tinted grey) with two steel rails 0.07 m wide, 1.435 m apart, metallic 0.8, roughness 0.4, and a sleeper pattern baked into the ballast texture (dark strips at 0.6 m pitch); road ribbons crossing it simply stay on top (level crossing). Add the class to ROAD_CLASSES/SURFACES and the tile size to materials.ROAD.
items.risk: BUILD_VERSION bump and map rebuild. Only worth doing if the data check finds rail inside the detail zone. Thin rails alias under TAA (give them at least pixel width at 40 m: about 3-4 cm per pixel, so 7 cm is about 2 px).

items.title: Bridges and culverts are not modelled: roads are draped on the bare-earth terrain, so any creek or highway crossing dips into the valley
items.current: Every road ribbon is ground(x, y) + 0.04 + 0.004 * priority sampled every 2 m (roads.py:137-149). The Overture columns 'road_flags' and 'level_rules' are requested (overture.py:87-89) but never read, so a bridge or a culvert crossing gets whatever height the terrain has below it. Creeks are burned into the ground class as WATER but the road is not interrupted.
items.real_world: Bare-earth lidar DEMs are meant to exclude bridge decks, so under a bridge the DEM shows the channel (stated from memory of the USGS lidar specification, not fetched, so unsourced); whether the DEM used here has been filled across bridges is unverified. The check is cheap: intersect road lines with water polygons and stream lines in the detail zone and measure the elevation range of the draped ribbon across each.
items.proposed_change: Read road_flags (is_bridge / is_tunnel; exact value names to be checked in the cached parquet) and level_rules in data.roads and add a bridge flag to Road. In roads_mesh, for flagged segments and for any segment that crosses a water polygon or a stream line wider than 3 m, replace the draped height between the two abutments by a straight or smoothstep profile between the abutment heights, add a 0.3 m thick deck and a low parapet, and lift the markings with it. Add a unit test on a synthetic DEM with a 4 m deep channel in scripts/drone_scene/test/test_world.py.
items.risk: BUILD_VERSION bump and map rebuild. The impact depends on a crossing lying near the route; find one offline first and use a --probe time near it (t<seconds>). Overture field names unverified. Thin parapets alias; keep them 0.3 m or more.

items.title: No overhead wires, transmission towers, water towers, grain elevators or turbines: Overture's infrastructure layer is never loaded
items.current: Both data.overture calls ask only for ['building','segment','water','land_use'] (and 'land' in the second). The reader already knows an 'infrastructure' type (overture.py:72, its own comment: 'bridges, power lines, towers, poles, pipelines'), but nothing requests or builds it. Existing item urban-yard-props-fences-poles mentions poles and street lamps only.
items.real_world: Computed: one pixel is 2.6 cm at 30 m range (0.8625 mrad per pixel), so a 1.5-2 cm conductor is a faint sub-pixel line that appears as a thin flickering streak, while a tower or water tank of 20-40 m height is a prominent vertical against the horizon. Which of these exist in west Ames and their heights are unverified and unsourced (check the Overture table offline before building).
items.proposed_change: Add 'infrastructure' to both overture() calls and a data.infrastructure() reader; build (a) poles every about 40 m along power lines (spacing unsourced) with a cross-arm, (b) catenary wires with a sag of about 2-3 % of the span as ribbons at least 1 pixel wide at 40 m (about 3-4 cm) to avoid flicker, (c) lattice towers and monopoles as simple prisms, (d) tall point structures (water tower, elevator) from the same layer or from building height >= 25 m. Include them in build.cruise_height obstacle top so the flight stays 15 m clear.
items.risk: BUILD_VERSION bump. Thin wires alias or shimmer under TAA. Data coverage unknown; the item may turn out to be near-empty for this route, so count features first. Overlaps urban-yard-props-fences-poles for poles: build both in one pass.

items.title: Every roof of a style carries the same clean shingle image: no age, streaks, stains, moss, patches or per-roof variation
items.current: textures.shingles() is a 2 m tile of 3-tab shingles: grey 0.30 x tab tone (+-12 %) x fine grain 12 % x a 5 % blotch at 0.4 m; the same seed 0 is used for all styles, which only differ by tint (materials.BUILDING). UVs are measured from each roof rectangle's own origin (buildings.py:209-212, tile 2 m from build.py:612), so every roof of a style starts at the same phase and looks identical. Flat roofs are one constant colour. There are no streaks below ridges, no algae on the shaded slope, no patches, no faded or soiled slopes.
items.real_world: Aged-roof reflectance and soiling statistics (for example the aged solar-reflectance data kept by LBNL/CRRC) were not fetched, so no number is quoted: unsourced. The visible fact is that roofs in an older suburb differ from each other in age and cleanliness, and shaded north slopes under trees are darker or greener.
items.proposed_change: Per building, derive an age a in [0, 1] from _hash01 and (1) offset and rotate the roof UV by another hash so no two roofs share a phase, (2) generate 4-6 shingle variants (different seeds, plus a 'weather' layer) per style, (3) in the weather layer add 0.3-1 m wide vertical streaks, an overall luminance shift of roughly -25 % to +15 % with age, and 1-3 rectangular repair patches per large roof, (4) tint the slope facing away from the sun slightly green-dark when the canopy grid shows trees within 8 m. Do this after urban-roof-albedo-palette fixes the base colours.
items.risk: BUILD_VERSION and TEXTURE_VERSION (materials.py:65) bumps; more material slots and larger texture memory. Weathering that is too strong lowers mean roof albedo and shifts exposure: compare with the NAIP squares.

items.title: Crop fields are uniform parallel rows edge to edge: no headland turn rows, grassed waterways, wet spots, tramlines or field entrances
items.current: crop_fields() labels connected crop areas, cuts them along roads and gives each field one row angle (long axis) and one phase (build.py:183-204, 273-279). The ground material for a whole field is the same 3.04 m row texture. Nothing inside a field varies in structure: no strip of different rows along the field edge, no drainage swale, no darker wet patch, no wheel tracks, no gap where a lane enters the field.
items.real_world: Not sourced in this session (web tools unreachable). Aerial views of Midwest row-crop fields commonly show a headland band along the edges, grassed waterways along drainage lines, tramlines and wet or stressed patches by mid-July; I could not confirm their frequency or widths for Ames, so check the NAIP squares from realism/reference.py before building anything.
items.proposed_change: (1) From the 2 m detail DEM (h_detail) compute flow accumulation inside each field and burn a 8-15 m wide MEADOW strip (widths unsourced) along strong flow paths. (2) Add a 6-12 m wide headland band inside each field edge using the existing per-face angle array in ground_materials with angle + 90 deg. (3) Add a crop texture variant with a darker 0.4 m wheel-track line every about 24 m, perpendicular to the rows (spacing unsourced) and pick it for alternate fields. (4) Compare the result with the NAIP nadir squares and drop whatever NAIP does not show for these fields.
items.risk: BUILD_VERSION and TEXTURE_VERSION bumps. Overlaps ground-crop-no-height-field-edges, ground-crop-tile-repeat-3m and ground-crop-canopy-closed: plan one crop rework. Only matters if farmland is a large share of the route (route_score favours mixed ground).

items.title: Near clip 0.01 m with far 10 km while coplanar road strips and markings are only 4-5 mm apart: possible z-fighting or shimmering lane lines
items.current: Onboard cameras use clipping_range (0.01, 10000.0) (quadcopter_pbr.py:619; the viewport copy at :306). Junction strips of different classes differ by 0.004 m per priority step, markings sit 0.005 m above the road (roads.py:137,153), flat roofs 0.05 m and notch roofs 0.02 m above the wall tops (buildings.py:288,304). Existing item camera-far-clip-horizon covers only the far plane.
items.real_world: Pipeline artefact, no real-world number. If the renderer resolves primary visibility with a standard 24-bit perspective depth buffer, the depth step is about z^2 / (near x 2^24) (textbook formula, not fetched): 1.2 cm at 44 m (the lowest image rows at cruise) and 3.4 cm at 75 m (image centre), which is larger than the 4-5 mm offsets, so markings and overlapped roads could flicker. Whether RTX real-time uses a rasterised depth buffer here is unverified; with ray-traced primary visibility there would be no problem.
items.proposed_change: Experiment first: render cruise_early and cruise_mid front stills plus a 2 s clip over a marked road with near = 0.01 (now), 0.1 and 0.25, and with --pathtracing (no depth buffer) as the control; score lane-marking continuity (broken or flickering pixels along a marking) and frame-to-frame difference. If the real-time modes show it and path tracing does not, set near to 0.1 m (the nearest ground the cameras see at take-off is about 0.2 m away) and raise the offsets to 2-3 cm (or scale them with distance), keeping the drone's own mount outside the clip range.
items.risk: A near clip of 0.1-0.25 m may clip the drone's own mount parts or the ground at touchdown (camera about 0.15-0.2 m above the ground, assumed): check the ground and final stills. Larger world offsets need a BUILD_VERSION bump; the clip test itself does not.
sources: depth-buffer resolution formula: textbook, not fetched

items.title: The take-off patio is spotless and empty: no furniture, grill, planters, hose or toys around the drone
items.current: The 3.6 x 4.2 m patio (SceneCfg.patio = (-1.6, 2.0, -2.2, 2.0)) holds herringbone pavers, a curb, a mulch bed with five shrubs and a maple (PLANTING), and 40 leaves; the drone is the only object on it. The first seconds of both videos (2 s idle, then the climb) show only this yard and the real house wall behind it.
items.real_world: Typical contents of a US backyard patio (table and chairs, a charcoal or gas grill, planters, a hose reel, a bin, children's toys) are common knowledge but unsourced here; the point is that a tidy bare patio is a first-impression tell. Distinct from vegetation-backyard-autumn-leaves-and-planting (leaves and shrubs) and from urban-yard-props-fences-poles (backyards across the map).
items.proposed_change: Add 6-10 props to scene.py beside PLANTING: a patio table with four chairs (about 0.8 m round table, chairs 0.45 m seats), a 0.6 m kettle grill, 2-3 terracotta planters with a plant from NVIDIA Vegetation, a coiled green hose and a plastic bin; use NVIDIA ArchVis props if present (names unverified; check the asset server) or simple primitives with the PBR helper preview_surface. Keep a 1.5 m radius around the drone clear. Place them on the paver top (cfg.patio_top + PaverSpec().top_rise).
items.risk: Asset availability and licence; props can occlude the front camera's first seconds (keep them off the 20 deg down view line close to the drone). Runtime scene only, no BUILD_VERSION bump. Interacts with camera-takeoff-landing-no-rotor-wash (light objects should move).

items.title: The hand-built yard is axis-aligned to the world and ignores where and how the real house stands
items.current: SceneCfg.patio is the rectangle x -1.6..2.0, y -2.2..2.0 in world axes and the foundation-planting bed is the strip x -3.8..-2.4 (scene.py:55-60) whatever the bearing of the real house. scene_cfg() in quadcopter_pbr.py rotates only the sky (sky_rotation_deg) and the sun. site.takeoff_candidates computes the direction away from the street (site.py:69-79) but the manifest (build.py:631-640) stores no yard orientation. The Overture house stands 9-14 m from the take-off, so patio edges are generally not parallel to the house wall and the 'bed against the house' may lie on the opposite side.
items.real_world: Patios are normally laid square to the house wall and the planting bed runs along the wall (common knowledge, unsourced). A rotated house next to a world-aligned patio is a visible inconsistency in the first seconds of both cameras.
items.proposed_change: In site.choose, return the direction from the take-off to the nearest house footprint and the angle of its nearest wall segment; write yard_yaw_deg into world.json (build.py manifest). In quadcopter_pbr.scene_cfg put /World/Scenery (patio, curb, bed, grass area, props, leaves, pavers) under a parent Xform rotated by yaw about Z so that the bed (-x side) faces the house and the patio edges are parallel to its wall; the drone and the circular terrain pad are at the origin so the rotation is safe. Keep the sun and sky in world coordinates (they are lights outside the Xform or counter-rotated). Add a test in test_world.py for the yaw choice.
items.risk: world.json gains a field and site.choose output changes, so BUILD_VERSION must be bumped (the cache key ignores nothing else) and the map rebuilt. Colliders, pavers.author_patio and the Poisson grass rectangle all live under one Xform so they rotate together; check the grass-to-terrain edge (ground-backyard-grass-patch-edge) after rotation.

items.title: Sports fields, courts, golf courses and playgrounds are plain lawn, and swimming pools use the same near-black mirror as ponds
items.current: OVERTURE_LAND_USE maps pitch, golf_course, fairway, playground, park, cemetery and recreation_ground all to LAWN (landcover.py:32-33). No infield dirt, court surface, line markings, bunkers or greens exist. OVERTURE_WATER (which names 'swimming_pool', landcover.py:42-43) is defined but never used; water_polygons() takes every polygon of the water table and ground_classes burns them all as WATER, rendered with materials.WATER colour (0.015, 0.025, 0.03), roughness 0.04 (materials.py:41). A backyard pool would therefore be a nearly black hole.
items.real_world: A swimming pool seen from above is a bright cyan-turquoise rectangle or kidney shape, one of the highest-contrast small objects in a suburb, and ball diamonds, tennis courts and golf bunkers have distinctive colours and white lines; exact reflectances and how many exist in the map are unsourced (count them offline first; NAIP squares show the colours).
items.proposed_change: (1) Add ground classes POOL and COURT. Split water polygons whose class is 'swimming_pool' into POOL with a bright blue-green material whose colour is taken from NAIP pixels inside the pool polygons (reference.py machinery); (2) for pitch polygons use the Overture/OSM sport tag where present: baseball infield = Soil texture with white 10 cm lines, tennis/basketball = flat acrylic colour sampled from NAIP, soccer/football = lawn with white lines drawn by the existing marking strip code in roads.py; (3) golf: fairway/green/bunker from the subclass, with bunkers as SAND; (4) playground = bark mulch or rubber surface.
items.risk: BUILD_VERSION and TEXTURE_VERSION bumps, map rebuild. Overlaps ground-water-mirror and urban-parking-lots-as-lawn: do the pool split after the water material is reworked. Check the number of such polygons in the detail zone first; if there are only a few, hand-tune them via the NAIP colours.
sources: pool and court colours and counts: unsourced

items.title: Sidewalks exist only where the map happens to have them; none are generated beside residential streets
items.current: A sidewalk or footway is drawn (1.6 m concrete ribbon, lift 0.044 m) only if Overture has a segment with subclass 'sidewalk' or class 'footway'/'sidewalk' (data.py:112, roads.py:27). Nothing is synthesized next to residential streets, so unmapped streets are bare asphalt ribbons directly against lawns. Existing items cover kerbs/gutters (urban-road-edge-gutter-crosswalk) and driveways (urban-driveways-missing), not sidewalks.
items.real_world: Most residential streets in a US city of Ames's kind have sidewalks on one or both sides, usually a 5 ft slab with expansion joints every few feet (common knowledge; widths and spacing unsourced). Seen from 40 m they are the thin light parallel lines that make a suburb read as a suburb.
items.proposed_change: Offline first: sum mapped sidewalk length against residential/tertiary road length in the detail zone from the cached Overture tables. Where a residential or tertiary street has no mapped footway within 12 m on a side and buildings stand within 40 m of it, synthesize a 1.5 m concrete ribbon offset w/2 + 2.5 m from the road centre line using roads.strip(), cut it where it meets a driveway apron, building, water or another road (leave a crossing at junctions), and add expansion joints each 1.5 m via a small groove in a concrete variant of the normal map. Build it together with the driveway and kerb items.
items.risk: BUILD_VERSION bump and map rebuild. False positives on rural roads (the building-density test guards this). Overlaps urban-driveways-missing and urban-road-edge-gutter-crosswalk: one coordinated roadside cross-section change is better than three.
sources: sidewalk prevalence, width and joint spacing: unsourced

result.notes:
Web access note: this session's WebSearch budget was already used up, and every WebFetch failed with a DNS error (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND, even for en.wikipedia.org), so I read no web page. I did not use curl or any other route around that. Because of that, no URL is cited. Every real-world number is either computed from values in the repo (the lucid.py pixel pitch and lens, vehicles.py mass) with the arithmetic shown, or marked 'unsourced'. Before the fleet builds a fix, a critic with working web access should replace each 'unsourced' with a URL (Ames July cloud and wind climatology, Iowa DOT traffic counts, USGS lidar bridge-deck treatment, Overture schema field and class names, NAIP resolution and year for Story County, roof ageing data).

Scope: I only read files (Read/Grep/Glob, plus one harmless line-count command at the start); I edited nothing, ran no project code, pushed nothing, and did not do the 'upload the agents to the IsaacSim repo' request, which is not part of this critic step (CLAUDE.md also says to ask before pushing).

Each item was checked against the code. Confirmed missing: sky clouds (WORLD_SKY is the clear pure-sky HDR), any animation of vegetation or traffic, rotor-wash effects, depth of field (pinhole cameras, hyperfocal_m unused), per-frame asset-loading waits, NAIP-derived colour (only used for comparison), railways (dropped in data.roads), bridges (road_flags and level_rules requested but unused), the infrastructure layer (never requested), per-roof weathering, field-scale structure, patio props, yard alignment with the real house, sports/pool classes (pools burn as the black water material; OVERTURE_WATER is dead code) and unmapped sidewalks.

Unverified premises the fleet should test cheaply first, offline on the PC from the cached Overture tables, before spending render time: (1) is there any rail line, bridge or water crossing, pool or pitch, and how much sidewalk within about 600 m of the chosen route; (2) whether RTX real-time uses a rasterised depth buffer (the camera-near-clip item); (3) whether asset streaming really lags in the record loop (add the assets_loading counter first).

Dependencies and overlaps: the three motion items (wind, traffic, rotor wash) and the streaming item can only be judged on a short video segment, so they depend on the existing camera-tool-probe-motion-segment. The sidewalk, driveway and kerb items should be one roadside rework. The NAIP item would supersede the fix suggested for ground-patch-quilt and helps ground-s2-bands-vs-camera-rgb. The cloud item must be coordinated with light-sky-hdr-wrong-sun-elevation (same HDR). Ordering suggestion by value per effort: camera-near-clip, camera-record-asset-streaming, urban-takeoff-patio-empty, urban-takeoff-yard-not-aligned, then the cloud sky, NAIP and roadside items.

Not turned into items because the evidence was thin: dual-carriageway roads get a double yellow centre line on each carriageway (roads.py:142-144; only matters if a trunk or motorway is in view, and I could not confirm that), cul-de-sac bulbs drawn as a ring of width 7.5 m around a lawn island (depends on how OSM maps them), and earth curvature (negligible below about 6 km). One idea outside render tests: the critics have only nadir NAIP references; a set of real oblique 40 m drone frames of a similar Iowa suburb in July (with a licence) would give them a ground truth for the front and back views.
